summary: A 1943 CT-2 timber lookout on East Pocket Knob near Sedona, registered in 2001, evacuated in 2014 and structure-protected during the 2026 Pocket Fire.

facts.design: CT-2 timber tower (Timber Engineering Corp.) with a 14 x 14 modified L-4 live-in cab with catwalk

access.note: Approach is by hiking the A. B. Young Trail into the Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness. No source read confirms public entry to the cab itself, and it is a working lookout.

visit.trail_note: A. B. Young Trail, about 2 miles one way with 33 switchbacks and about 1,950 ft of elevation gain

events.note: Timber Engineering Corp. CT-2 timber tower with a 14 x 14 modified L-4 live-in cab
Plans quoted from a 1948 Tucson Daily Citizen item called for radio lookout sets at Elden, East Pocket and Baker Butte
Registered April 1, 2001; nominated by Dave Lorenz, Director, AZ/NM FFLA
Slide Fire threatened about 100 Oak Creek Canyon structures, including this tower; tower evacuated May 20, 2014
Pocket Fire ignited June 19, 2026; structure protection maintained at East Pocket Lookout Tower; no structures or homes lost in the fire

evidence.supports: 1943 CT-2 tower by Timber Engineering Corp.; 14 x 14 live-in cab with catwalk
evidence.quote: Another of the rare CT-2 towers (this one manufactured by Timber Engineering Corp. in 1943), East Pocket Lookout has a 14' x 14' live-in cab with catwalk.

evidence.supports: modified L-4 cab; elevation 7,196 ft; Peaks Ranger District
evidence.quote: Set on an elevation of 7,196' on the Peaks Ranger District of the Coconino, it is an R-3 modified L-4 cab.

evidence.supports: 1943 construction of ring-connected CT-2 timber tower with 14 x 14 modified L-4 live-in cab
evidence.quote: 1943: A ring-connected CT-2 timber tower with a 14 x 14 modified L-4 live-in cab was constructed.

evidence.supports: built in 1943; one of only two wooden fire lookouts remaining in Arizona
evidence.quote: The lookout was built in 1943 and is one of only two wooden fire lookouts remaining in Arizona.

evidence.supports: about 7.5 miles north of Sedona, in the Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness
evidence.quote: East Pocket Knob is located 7.5 miles (12.1 km) north of Sedona in the Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness

evidence.supports: land managed by Coconino National Forest
evidence.quote: on land managed by Coconino National Forest

evidence.supports: trail to the tower is about two miles one way with 33 switchbacks and 1,950 ft gain; hiking route
evidence.quote: Hiking the strenuous A. B. Young Trail to the fire lookout tower at the summit covers two miles (one-way) with 33 switchbacks and 1,950 feet of elevation gain.

evidence.supports: trail first built in the 1880s to access grazing pastures
evidence.quote: The trail was originally built by C.S. (Bear) Howard in the 1880s to access grazing pastures on the plateau,

evidence.supports: trail rebuilt by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s
evidence.quote: then it was reconstructed in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps as supervised by A.B. Young.

evidence.supports: 1948 newspaper item: plans for radio lookout sets at Elden, East Pocket and Baker Butte
evidence.quote: Present plans call for lookout sets to be installed at Elden, East Pocket and Baker Butte stations.

evidence.supports: 1948 item: radios will be used to help fight fires in the Coconino
evidence.quote: Radios will be used to help fight fires in the Coconino national forest.

evidence.supports: May 2014 Slide Fire threatened Oak Creek Canyon structures; tower evacuated
evidence.quote: May 20, 2014: The Slide Fire was reported to be burning northward in Oak Creek Canyon jeopardizing approximately 100 structures, including the lookout tower on East Pocket. As a result of this threat the tower was evacuated.

evidence.supports: nominated by Dave Lorenz, Director, AZ/NM FFLA
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Pocket Fire ignited June 19, 2026, about 7 miles north of Sedona
evidence.quote: The Pocket Fire ignited June 19, 2026, approximately 7 miles north of Sedona, Arizona

evidence.supports: structure protection maintained at East Pocket Lookout Tower during the Pocket Fire
evidence.quote: Structure protection was maintained at Slide Rock State Park, Seven Canyons Golf Club, the Enchantment Resort, and East Pocket Lookout Tower.

evidence.supports: no structures or homes lost in the Pocket Fire
evidence.quote: Though there remained a threat throughout the Pocket Fire, no structures or homes were ever lost.

sources.title: Recent Large Wildfires
sources.publisher: Coconino National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Current staffing is unconfirmed; no dated staffing record was found. Access is a judgment: the trail is a public hike, but entry to the cab is not confirmed, so the level is set to restricted. The Pocket Fire fate comes from the USFS page. NHLR gives the Peaks Ranger District, while the 2026 fire page places the fire on the Red Rock Ranger District, so the current district is not settled. The 80-ft wooden height appears only in a search snippet, and the Sedona city and AZ Daily Sun pages failed (403, 429), so no height is recorded. Read budget was exceeded (about 9 page reads) to confirm the 2026 fire fate.
